reid.notes: Root-caused from results/identity_audit.jsonl: Person_003's FIRST cam1->cam2 jump matched at color_similarity=0.59 (weak -- likely a different person), while Person_001's correct cam1->cam2 match had color_similarity=0.64. Once that weak Person_003 jump was accepted, its embedding entered the rolling prototype pool, so every later cam2 match compared against a contaminated (multi-person) pool and looked artificially confident. min_color_similarity (0.55->0.62) and camera_thresholds['2'] (0.68->0.72) were both set to sit strictly between 0.59 and 0.64/0.7369, blocking the contaminating first jump while leaving Person_001's real match untouched. If this still misfires, capture the exact frame + identity_audit.jsonl line for the wrong merge so the threshold can be re-targeted precisely instead of widening it blindly.
